name: msteams
description: Microsoft Teams bot (Azure Bot Framework): message it in a personal chat, group chat or team channel and it answers from Elowen AI. Incoming activities arrive on the daemon webhook /hooks/msteams/messages (validated against Microsoft's JWT); replies, typing indicators and images go out through the Bot Connector REST API. Slash commands (/model, /reasoning, /display, /new, /help) with Adaptive Card pickers, AskUserQuestion as tappable cards, live tool activity, proactive cron/tick pushes and a downloadable Teams app package. Chat tools: conversation & member info, member lists, list conversations and person lookup; plus send a message to any chat, message a person proactively by e-mail or name (the bot opens the 1:1 chat itself), and raw connector access. Each rolePolicy admits an Entra object ID / UPN / conversation ID and may add room instructions; project and tool permissions always come from the sender's linked Elowen account.

configSchema.label: Connection
configSchema.hint: Azure Bot credentials. Setup: 1) Entra admin center → App registrations → New registration (single tenant) → copy the Application (client) ID and tenant ID, then Certificates & secrets → New client secret. 2) Azure portal → Create an Azure Bot bound to that app ID; set the messaging endpoint to https://<your-domain>/hooks/msteams/messages and enable the Microsoft Teams channel. 3) Download the app package (button above) and upload it in the Teams admin center → Manage apps.

configSchema.label: Microsoft App ID
configSchema.hint: The Entra app registration's Application (client) ID — also the bot ID in the Azure Bot resource.

configSchema.label: Client secret
configSchema.hint: A client secret from the app registration (Certificates & secrets). Used to call the Bot Connector API.

configSchema.label: Tenant ID
configSchema.hint: Your Entra Directory (tenant) ID — the bot authenticates against this tenant (single-tenant app registration).

configSchema.label: Personal-chat Microsoft sign-in
configSchema.hint: Any enabled Member account from this tenant may sign in from a personal chat and receive its own Elowen account. The linked account's projects and tool permissions then apply wherever that person writes, including shared channels and threads. Access and refresh tokens remain in Bot Framework Token Service.

configSchema.label: OAuth connection name
configSchema.hint: The exact connection name configured on the Azure Bot resource. Use the Microsoft Entra ID v2 provider, this tenant, delegated Microsoft 365 scopes, redirect URI https://token.botframework.com/.auth/web/redirect, and leave Token Exchange URL empty.

configSchema.label: Microsoft single sign-on
configSchema.hint: Sign in to the Elowen web interface with a Microsoft account from this tenant.

configSchema.label: Enable Microsoft sign-in
configSchema.hint: Shows Microsoft sign-in on the login page when the public redirect base is configured correctly.

configSchema.label: Public Elowen URL
configSchema.hint: Absolute public HTTPS URL without a path, for example https://elowen.example.com. Register this URL plus /api/auth/sso/microsoft/callback as the redirect URI in the Entra app.

configSchema.label: Account provisioning
configSchema.hint: Controls whether new accounts may be created on first sign-in. Entire tenant allows any enabled tenant member and requires the Microsoft Graph application permission User.Read.All with tenant admin consent; without it, provisioning is refused.

configSchema.label: Link existing accounts by e-mail
configSchema.hint: On first sign-in, the Microsoft identity may link to exactly one existing account with the same e-mail. The matched account may be an administrator. The e-mail claim is not a verified, immutable identifier; after linking, the durable identity uses the Entra object ID.

configSchema.label: Default projects for new accounts
configSchema.hint: Projects assigned only when a new account is provisioned.

configSchema.label: Allowed models for new accounts
configSchema.hint: Models the new account may use. Empty leaves its personal model allow-list unrestricted.

configSchema.label: Preferred model for new accounts
configSchema.hint: Preferred model selected for the new account. Empty leaves it unset.

configSchema.label: Granted plugins for new accounts
configSchema.hint: Grant-gated plugins available to the new account.

configSchema.label: Granted tools for new accounts
configSchema.hint: Tools the new account may use. Leaving this empty grants none, so the account reaches its first turn with no plugin tool until an administrator grants some.

configSchema.label: Microsoft 365 tools
configSchema.hint: Delegated Graph tools always act as the signed-in person and are available only inside that person's personal Teams chat. Tokens remain in Bot Framework Token Service.

configSchema.label: Microsoft 365 access
configSchema.hint: Read only blocks every external mutation. Read and write still previews each mutation until the agent explicitly commits the exact operation.

configSchema.label: Microsoft file transfer limit
configSchema.hint: Maximum file size downloaded from or uploaded to Microsoft 365 in one tool call. Larger uploads use a resumable Microsoft upload session.

configSchema.label: App name in Teams
configSchema.hint: Name of the app and of the bot in the downloadable app package — what people see in the organisation's Teams catalog and in /help. Empty = Elowen. Set it when that name collides with another app already in the catalog.

configSchema.label: Publisher name in Teams
configSchema.hint: Publisher shown on the app package (the manifest's developer name). Empty = the configured app name.

configSchema.label: App icon in Teams
configSchema.hint: Absolute path on the server to a PNG of exactly 192×192 pixels, used as the app icon in the downloadable app package. Empty = a plain coloured square. The file is read when the package is downloaded; if it is missing or has the wrong size, the download fails with the reason instead of producing a package Teams would reject.

configSchema.label: Notification conversation
configSchema.hint: Where proactive messages (cron/tick results) are posted. Empty = no proactive pushes.

configSchema.label: Reaching people first
configSchema.hint: The bot can start a chat with someone instead of only answering. It remembers everyone it meets (name, Entra object ID, UPN and their 1:1 chat) from incoming messages and conversation rosters — no extra Microsoft permission — and TeamsMessagePerson writes to them by e-mail or name. The settings below are only needed for people the bot has never seen.

configSchema.label: Microsoft Graph lookup
configSchema.hint: Off: the bot can only write to people it has already met in Teams. On: an unknown e-mail is resolved against the tenant directory and the Teams app is installed for that person so a chat can be opened. Requires the APPLICATION permissions User.ReadBasic.All and TeamsAppInstallation.ReadWriteSelfForUser.All with tenant admin consent. Directory avatars additionally use ProfilePhoto.Read.All; without it the workspace falls back to the linked Elowen account avatar.

configSchema.label: Teams catalog app ID
configSchema.hint: The app's ID in the organisation's Teams catalog (Teams admin center → Manage apps → the uploaded Elowen app). Needed to install the app for a user who does not have it yet; leave empty if the app is deployed by Teams app policy.

configSchema.label: Replies & behavior
configSchema.hint: When and how the bot answers.

configSchema.label: Respond without mention
configSchema.hint: On: in group chats the bot answers every message from a mapped sender. Off: it only answers when @mentioned. In team channels, messages without a mention are delivered only after ChannelMessage.Read.Group consent is active.

configSchema.label: Tool activity
configSchema.hint: What the progress message shows while the agent works: nothing, tool status lines, or status plus live output tails.

configSchema.label: Answer delivery
configSchema.hint: Final posts one reply when the turn ends; live streams the answer into a message as it is written.

configSchema.label: Tool output detail
configSchema.hint: How much of each tool's result the progress message keeps once the tool finishes.

configSchema.label: Tool message layout
configSchema.hint: Single keeps one edited progress message; per-tool posts a message per tool call.

configSchema.label: Replace tool activity with answer
configSchema.hint: Show one live progress message while the agent works, then replace that same message with the final answer. No message is deleted; live-answer and per-tool layouts are overridden.

configSchema.label: Processing reactions
configSchema.hint: Shows processing status using reactions on the incoming message.

configSchema.label: Runtime footer
configSchema.hint: Append a small "model · context %" line under the final reply.

configSchema.label: Show reasoning
configSchema.hint: Stream the model's reasoning into the progress message (extended-thinking models). Off by default — it's usually noise.

configSchema.label: Service language
configSchema.hint: Language of the bot's own service messages (errors, command replies). The agent itself answers in the user's language.

configSchema.label: Conversation
configSchema.hint: Context loading and image routing.

configSchema.label: Conversation history backfill
configSchema.hint: How many recent messages a brand-new conversation loads as context (0 = off, max 100). The bot always falls back to what it witnessed; with ChannelMessage.Read.Group consent, a channel thread can also be read back from Microsoft Graph.

configSchema.label: Read every channel message
configSchema.hint: Adds the ChannelMessage.Read.Group resource-specific permission to the downloadable app package, so in a team where the app is installed the bot SEES every channel message instead of only @mentions — that is what fills the history backfill above. A team owner consents when the package is installed or updated in that team (no tenant admin needed), so this setting alone changes nothing until the new package is uploaded and the app updated in the team.

configSchema.label: Vision model
configSchema.hint: Model used for turns that carry image attachments (must support vision). Empty = the chat's normal model.

configSchema.label: Media limits
configSchema.hint: Caps on inbound/outbound images and how long a pending question stays open.

configSchema.label: Max inbound image size
configSchema.hint: Largest image attachment (bytes) the bot downloads for vision.

configSchema.label: Max images per message
configSchema.hint: How many image attachments in a single incoming message the bot sends to the vision model.

configSchema.label: Max images per reply
configSchema.hint: How many generated images the bot attaches to a single outgoing reply.

configSchema.label: Role policies
configSchema.hint: Decide which Teams senders the bot admits and optionally add room instructions.

configSchema.label: Role policies
configSchema.hint: First matching policy admits the sender. The ID is the sender's Entra object ID (a GUID), their UPN/email, a whole conversation ID (admits everyone in that chat), or * for every sender — keep a * policy last, below the named entries it would otherwise swallow. `admin` enables room-administration slash commands and trusted-room context only. Project and tool permissions always come from the sender's linked Elowen account; an admitted unlinked sender receives the existing sign-in card and no brain turn.
